newsitem.title: USA: UI says regulations contribute to decline.
newsitem.headline: UI says regulations contribute to decline.

text.p: United Illuminating said Monday it expects revenues from retail operations to decline in 1997 because of a five year rate reduction plan it agreed to implement under an order set out by the Department of Public Utility Control.
The company said in a statement that the order would in turn accelerate the recovery of certain "regulatory" assets beginning with deferred conservation costs.

United Illuminated said the order allowed the company to return on common stock equity invested in a base utility rate above 11.5 percent through 2001. One third of the earnings will be returned to customers through rate reductions; one third applied to more rapid amortization of its regulatory assets and one third will be retained by shareholders.

Retail revenues, the company said, are likely to fall by $15 million due to reductions in customer bills. But the rate reductions are expected to be offset by $3 million less in conservation spending.
United Illuminating said it expects energy generation from its two nuclear power plants to decline in 1997.

The company's Seabrook Unit 1, which operated at 97 percent of capacity in 1996, well above normal, will have downtime in 1997 for refueling, causing them to purchase or generate energy using higher cost fuels, which in turn will lead to an expected $3 million more 1997 fuel expenses.

The company said its Millstone Unit 3 nuclear reactor remains out of service since March 30, 1996. The company expects that to continue until the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reviews operations. In addition, company's board of directors retired the Connecticut Yankee reactor. That move is expected to add $4.5 million to fuel expenses.
United Illuminating expects to reduce expenses for its nuclear generating units by roughly $10 million in 1998 due to costs declines in its Seabrook and now retired Connecticut Yankee facilities.
